title: Agreeee (JP: 利用規約に同意したい, 'I Want to Agree to the Terms of Service')
genre: Puzzle / comedic minigame collection / 'rage' challenge (meta terms-of-service satire)
release_date: 2025-12-05 JST (Steam, PC only; shown as 2025-12-04 on some US-time listings) [CONFIRMED – Automaton, Game*Spark, Steam store]
team_size: 1 (solo / 個人ゲームクリエイター) [CONFIRMED – Automaton ('個人ゲームクリエイターのべすとまん氏'); Wikipedia 'indie developer Vestman']
country: Japan [CONFIRMED – Japanese individual creator per Automaton / Wikipedia ('Japanese puzzle video game')]
developer_background: Japanese individual game creator who self-publishes on Steam (developer and publisher both listed as べすとまん). Steam sells it in a bundle with another title, 'Malware' (the dev's own earlier game – not verified). Stated aim: 'use the game to draw people's attention to the fact that nobody reads the terms of service' (Wikipedia).
business_model: Premium, cheap: $4.99 list [Steambase]; ¥580 incl. tax at launch with a 20% launch discount [Automaton/Game*Spark]; 20% sale to $3.99 seen on ~2026-10-08 [Steam store]; bundle with 'Malware' (~$5.17).
units_or_downloads: 10,000 copies on 2025-12-27, 20,000 on 2026-01-02 and 30,000+ on 2026-01-07 [CONFIRMED – developer announcement via Automaton 2026-01-08; Wikipedia]. Current (2026-10-08): ~45,000–60,000 [ESTIMATE – Boxleiter ~1,150–1,290 reviews × 40–50 (cheap, streamer-driven, Japanese audience with low review propensity)]. No later official milestone found.
peak_concurrent_players: 618 all-time peak on 2026-01-07 [ESTIMATE – Steambase]. ~100 CCU right after launch rising to ~500 on 2025-12-27 [CONFIRMED – Automaton/Wikipedia]. ~24 CCU in a recent snapshot [Steambase].
steam_reviews: 1,156 reviews, 74% positive, 'Mostly Positive' (Steam store snapshot, ~Oct 2026; other snapshots 1,139 @ 74% and 1,073 @ 75%); WASDland lists 1,284 (950 positive / 334 negative ≈ 74%). Recent 30 days: 66–72% of ~18–21 reviews.
implied_review_multiplier: n/a (no review count found for 2026-01-07; 30,000 ÷ current ~1,156 reviews = 26 is a floor, the true same-date ratio is higher)
gross_revenue: ~$110k by 2026-01-07 [ESTIMATE – 30,000 confirmed units × ~$3.70 (¥580 launch price ≈ $3.70; $4.99 × 0.75 = $3.74)]; ~$165k–$225k to date [ESTIMATE – 45k–60k units × ~$3.70]. No tracker revenue estimate found.
net_revenue: ~$70k by 2026-01-07; ~$105k–$145k to date [ESTIMATE – gross × (1 − 30% Steam cut) × 0.93 refunds]; self-published, no publisher split.
production_cost: No disclosed figure; dev time unknown. Illustrative opportunity cost ~$36k–$72k [ESTIMATE – 1 person × 6–12 months × $6k/month Japan rate; ≥6 months is suggested by press coverage from June 2025 and the Sept 2025 demo].
development_time: no data (lower bound ~6 months: covered by Denfaminicogamer around June 2025, demo 2025-09-22, release 2025-12-05)
why_popular: Brilliant one-line hook: to start the 'game' you just have to tick 'Agree' on 12 terms-of-service articles – but each checkbox is sabotaged by one of 100+ absurd, punishing minigames (pinball, whack-a-mole, bomb defusal, etc.), parodying the fact that nobody reads ToS. Relatable satire + rage-game frustration + variety = perfect 'endurance stream' (耐久配信) material for Japanese streamers and VTubers; sales accelerated over the holidays as streams spread (10k → 30k in 11 days).
marketing_channels: Free Steam demo (Sept 2025); Japanese streamers and VTubers doing endurance streams/let's plays (YouTube/Twitch/Niconico); Japanese game press (Automaton, Game*Spark incl. a picture-diary feature, Denfaminicogamer, Famitsu, gamebiz); dev's X/Twitter milestone posts; very low price.
engine: no data (not found in Steam/press snippets after 3+ searches)
art_style: Simple 2D UI-parody presentation (fake terms-of-service screens and a fake 'Doki-Doki Action Game' title) with assorted simple 2D minigames.
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: generate dozens of small 2D minigames fast (each is a tiny self-contained loop – ideal for Claude Code), write the ToS parody text in several languages, make simple 2D art, UI, SFX and jingles. | AI cannot: come up with the meta-joke and comedic timing, tune difficulty so it is infuriating-but-fair for streams, curate which of 100+ gags land, or reach Japanese streamers/VTubers. 100+ minigames is volume, not complexity, which is why it is a 4 rather than a 5. | Toolset: Claude Code + Godot 4 or Unity 2D, Midjourney/Scenario/Retro Diffusion for 2D art, ElevenLabs SFX, Suno jingles, GodotSteam/Steamworks.NET; JP/EN localisation drafted by Claude and checked by a native speaker.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 2–4 weeks for ~20 minigames, ~$100–$300 (Claude Pro, image/audio subs, $100 Steam Direct). Excludes developer living costs.
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 2–4 months for 100+ minigames, ~$800–$3,000 (subs, art polish, native-speaker localisation check, streamer outreach/keys). Excludes developer living costs.

sources.title: Game*Spark – 『利用規約に同意したい』正式リリース (2025-12-05)
Game*Spark – 吉田輝和の絵日記: 『利用規約に同意したい』 (2026-01-05)

data_conflicts: Release date 2025-12-05 (JST, press) vs 2025-12-04 (US-time listings) – used 12-05. Peak CCU: ~500 on 2025-12-27 (Automaton/Wikipedia) vs 618 on 2026-01-07 (Steambase, later, so both are consistent). Review count varies by snapshot/aggregator: 1,073–1,156 (Steam) vs 1,284 (WASDland). Price: $4.99 list (Steambase) vs ¥580 (launch-discounted JP price). The brief described it as 'viral among VTubers'; press confirms streamer popularity (endurance streams) but I found no article naming specific VTubers.
notes: Proof that a tiny, cheap, single-joke game with a universally relatable premise can sell 30k copies in a month through Japanese streaming culture. Mixed-ish 74% reviews show the rage/'kichiku' difficulty divides buyers. Engine and dev time remain unknown.
